- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history, then gradually correct — suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after prolonged upward trends.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- Model reacts too slowly to sudden drops in history — underestimates short-term reversals.
- When history contains a strong upward trend, model overreacts with exaggerated peaks, then fails to smoothly decay back to mean.
- Correction should involve dampening early forecast values and introducing a decay factor for recent spikes.
- Use a moving average or exponential smoothing with higher decay for recent history to reduce overfitting to recent highs.
- Adjust forecast downward if the last 5–7 days show a clear downward trend or price correction.
- Avoid extrapolating upward trends beyond 2–3 days without checking for mean reversion signals.
